newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch govt borrowing requirement to fall in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch govt borrowing requirement to fall in 1997.

text.p: The Dutch central government borrowing requirement is expected to fall to 33.5 billion guilders in 1997 from 35.1 billion guilders in 1996, according to Finance Ministry figures released with the 1997 budget.
The borrowing requirement is made up of the gap between government spending and revenues -- the real budget deficit -- plus redemptions of government bonds issued in the past.
The Finance Ministry's figures show that the real deficit is set to rise to 21.0 billion guilders in 1997 from an exceptionally low 13.4 billion guilders in 1996.
Redemptions of previously issued government debt are set to fall to 12.5 billion guilders in 1997 from 21.6 billion guilders this year.

As a result of borrowing patterns in the past, redemptions are relatively low in 1996 and 1997 but will jump to between 30 and 50 billion guilders a year in the period 1998-2001 before stabilising at 20 to 30 billion guilders in 2002-2007.
The Finance Ministry said its borrowing policy in 1997 would continue to favour the creation of large, liquid fixed-maturity bond issues with a minimum size of some 10 billion guilders.
Some two thirds of all outstanding Dutch government debt already meets these criteria and by the year 2000 this figure will rise to around 95 percent, it added.
The ministry said it had decided to break with its policy of "front-loading", by which it had previously covered up to 75 percent of its borrowing needs in the first half of the year.
Changes in international financial markets and in Dutch public finances meant it was no longer necessary to issue most government bonds early in the year, it said.
The front-loading policy has resulted in a concentration of redemptions and interest payments in the first half of the year.
The ministry said that from 1997 it would look into ways of redressing this imbalance by shifting more of its interest and redemption commitments into the second half of the year.
In 1996 the government will not have to issue bonds to cover the full 35.1 billion guilder borrowing requirement.
The Finance Ministry said 1.1 billion guilders in surplus funds generated by the 1995 sale of shares in phones and post group PTT Nederland would be used to reduce 1996 borrowing.
